Marissa — adding technical answers inline below (I pasted relevant question headings from Priya's SSQ to keep traceability).

> Which Redwood services process customer PII for our integration?
- Answer: The default hosted path is Redwood Hosted API (multi-tenant inference). For customers requiring isolation or specific residency, we support Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. We'll mark each SSQ row with applicable deployment mode.

> Provide a list of subprocessors and processing locations.
- Answer: Current subprocessors (short roster):
  • Cloud provider infra (us-west-2, eu-west-1) — compute & ephemeral storage for hosted API (contracted subprocessor).
  • Managed logging/monitoring provider — telemetry retention per contract; logs are scrubbed for PII by default and retained per customer configuration.
  • KMS provider — hosts encryption keys in HSM-backed regions (we publish key location per customer).
  • Metrics/analytics vendor — processes aggregated telemetry only.
  Full roster + per-vendor processing descriptions attached as the "subprocessor_roster.csv" (we'll include in the SSQ package).

> How do you enforce access controls and RBAC?
- Answer: Access is role-based via our IAM tied to SSO (SCIM). Production access requires approval workflows, periodic reviews, and just-in-time elevated sessions for engineers. All privileged access is logged and audited.

> Dataflow / pseudonymization / KMS custody
- Answer: See attached dataflow_diagram_v2.png and kms-diagram.png. Short summary: PII fields are segmented at ingestion; we support optional tokenization/pseudonymization in the proxy layer. KMS keys for customer data are customer-specific for Dedicated/Private; for hosted, we offer an HSM-backed key custody option (Bring-Your-Own-Key possible via our KMS integrations).

> Residency and cross-border transfers
- Answer: For hosted customers, inference may route to the nearest compatible region by default; we offer routing constraints to keep processing within region where required. For strict residency, Dedicated/Private deployments are the recommended path and we'll include that language in the DPA excerpt.

I'll attach the two diagrams and a short CSV roster for inclusion in the SSQ. If they need signed attestations for certain subprocessors, we can surface SOC 2 or equivalent artifacts under an NDA/secure upload.

Attachments referenced: dataflow_diagram_v2.png, kms-diagram.png, subprocessor_roster.csv

-Karthik
Principal Privacy Engineer — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
